defs: Dynamic programming
Algorithms computing values/optimal policies from a perfect MDP model via Bellman updates.
Iterative policy evaluation
Repeated expectation backups converging to v_π.
Expected update
Uses all next states weighted by the model, not a sample.
Value iteration
Repeated optimality (max) backups; greedy policy at the end.
Asynchronous DP
In-place updates in any order using latest values.
Policy improvement theorem
If q_π(s, π′(s)) ≥ v_π(s) ∀s then v_π′ ≥ v_π.
Policy iteration
Alternate full evaluation and greedy improvement until stable.
Modified policy iteration
Truncated evaluation (a few sweeps) between improvements.
GPI
Interaction of evaluation and improvement toward (π*, v*).
Curse of dimensionality
State count grows exponentially with state variables.
confused: Max over actions vs average under π.
Two arrays vs updating one array immediately.
Few expensive iterations vs many cheap sweeps.
All successors weighted by p vs one sampled successor.
General pattern vs one specific (coarse) instance.
recall.minute: Dynamic programming solves MDPs with a known model by turning Bellman equations into updates. Iterative policy evaluation sweeps V(s) ← Σπ Σp[r + γV(s′)] until Δ < θ; in a 4×4 grid the greedy policy is optimal after a few sweeps even before values converge. Value iteration applies V(s) ← maxₐ Σp[r + γV(s′)] and extracts a greedy policy. Race car (Cool, Warm, Overheated; slow/fast; γ = 0.9): V₁ = (2, 1), V₂ = (3.35, 2.35), v* = (15.5, 14.5), policy fast in Cool, slow in Warm; our synchronous run needs 49 sweeps for Δ < 0.01, in-place updates 40 (V₂ = (3.755, 3.545)). Policy iteration evaluates fully then improves greedily, justified by the policy improvement theorem: (slow, slow) is worth (10, 10); switching Cool to fast (q = 11) gives (15.5, 14.5), which is stable. PI takes few expensive steps, VI many cheap ones. Generalised policy iteration — evaluation and improvement interacting until the policy is greedy w.r.t. its own values — underlies DP, Monte Carlo control, TD control and actor–critic.
